teaching.hint: Once you decide to earn points from a value, what reason would there be to leave another copy of it unchosen?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Positive equal values can be bundled into one reward; choosing a value conflicts only with adjacent values on the number line.
solution_outline.approach: Aggregate reward x times its frequency for each value x. Sweep values in order, keeping the best total through the preceding one and two values; choose between skipping x and adding its bundle to the optimum through x-2.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The best-prefix state is the maximum reward using values no greater than the current value; missing values have zero reward.
solution_outline.correctness: Any optimum either excludes x or includes it. In the latter case taking all copies is beneficial and excludes x-1, leaving exactly an independent optimum through x-2. Both alternatives are achievable, so induction over values proves the recurrence and final optimum.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n+M) time and O(M) space for frequencies up to maximum value M; the DP itself needs O(1) state.
solution_outline.pitfall: Applying a neighbor conflict to adjacent array positions instead of neighboring values solves a different problem.

common_wrong_turns: Applying a neighbor conflict to adjacent array positions instead of neighboring values solves a different problem.
source_fidelity_notes: Clarified that other equal occurrences are retained after choosing x; retained positivity and bounded value domain.
